citations.narrative:
Two Yorkies did not have official identification. The licensee states that the dogs are 4 months old. The dogs were not
wearing collars with tags and the licensee confirmed by scanning that they were not microchipped. Identification is
important in order to maintain inventory of animals, as well as tracing medical, breeding, and sales records, or in cases of
theft or loss. Correct by ensuring all live dogs held on the premises shall be identified by an official tag of the type
described in 2.51 affixed to the animal’s neck by means of a collar or by a distinctive and legible tattoo or microchip as
accepted by the Administrator. Correct by: June 23, 2026

The facility is not maintaining complete medical records for all of the vaccines required by the Animal Welfare Act and for
doses of monthly heartworm preventative, which are required in the Program of Vet Care. Records for heartworm
prevention, parvovirus vaccination, and distemper vaccination in all adult dogs were not able to be reviewed at the time of
inspection because they had not been adequately recorded. Complete medical records allow APHIS inspectors to ensure
the facility is following their written program of vet care and the Animal Welfare Act. Correct by ensuring dealers keep
copies of medical records for dogs and make the records available for APHIS inspection. In addition to the identification of
the animal, complete medical records must include the names of all vaccines and treatments administered and the dates
of administration. Correct by: June 23, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
Additional Inspectors:
Emily Steele, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
